The CINAHL, Cochrane, Embase, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Sciences databases were searched for quantitative studies published between 2014 and 2025. Eligible studies included children and adolescents with cancer who received CAT. A total of 4860 records were identified, of which 26 studies met the inclusion criteria and were synthesized narratively. CAT was generally associated with reductions in anxiety, depression, stress, distress, fear, procedural pain, and emotional discomfort, and with improvements in coping, emotional regulation, sleep quality, relaxation, happiness, and quality of life. A smaller subset of studies reported potential benefits for physiological markers, including heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, cortisol levels, hemodynamic status, and hematologic indicators. CAT may support psychological well-being, symptom relief, and stress regulation among children with cancer and may be a useful complement to supportive care in pediatric oncology, although further rigorous trials using standardized outcomes are needed.

artigos.titulo: Drivers of zoonotic spillover at human-domestic animal-wildlife interfaces: a multi-species model incorporating wildlife chronic stress
artigos.autores: Stafford E, Guo J, Fransson P et al.
artigos.destaque: These findings highlight the importance of maintaining ecological conditions that reduce chronic physiological stress in wildlife populations and integrating physiological and ecological data into epidemiological modelling. Such models can inform both bottom-up interventions targeting domestic animals and top-down strategies that sustain resilient wildlife communities and, thereby, mitigate zoonotic spillover.

resumo.texto: Zoonotic disease emergence at the wildlife-domestic animal-human interface results from a complex interplay of ecological, physiological and anthropogenic factors. Here, we have developed a multi-environment, multi-host compartmental model to identify key drivers of spillover risk across urban, rural and natural environments. The framework incorporates heterogeneous host populations, inter-species contacts and host movement, and includes wildlife chronic stress as one factor influencing susceptibility, transmissibility and recovery. Sensitivity analyses show that domestic animal populations at agricultural interfaces strongly amplify spillover risk through their recovery dynamics and per-contact transmission probabilities, while within-wildlife transmission across environments also shapes system dynamics. Chronic stress effects can further increase spillover risk, and the model indicates that reducing wildlife stress alongside improving domestic animal health and management can markedly lower the likelihood of cross-species transmission. These findings highlight the importance of maintaining ecological conditions that reduce chronic physiological stress in wildlife populations and integrating physiological and ecological data into epidemiological modelling. Such models can inform both bottom-up interventions targeting domestic animals and top-down strategies that sustain resilient wildlife communities and, thereby, mitigate zoonotic spillover.

artigos.titulo: Forest walking promoted the psychological and physiological health of postmenopausal women
artigos.autores: Shen JL, Chiang MR, Tsai MJ et al.
artigos.destaque: In conclusion, forest-based walking interventions elicit more favorable physiological and psychological responses than urban park walking. By enhancing parasympathetic activation, immune function, and psychological well-being, forest walking serves as a practical, evidence-based strategy to promote holistic health in postmenopausal women.

resumo.texto: There is growing interest in lifestyle-based strategies supporting postmenopausal women's psychological well-being and physiological resilience. Because evidence regarding natural environments remains scarce for this demographic, this study examined acute psychophysiological responses to 60-minute walking sessions in forest versus urban contexts. Twenty-four physically inactive postmenopausal women (≥50 years) completed a within-subject trial. Assessments included psychological questionnaires, heart rate variability (HRV), mucosal immune biomarkers (salivary immunoglobulin A [SIgA], lactoferrin, α-amylase), and stress markers (cortisol, nitric oxide [NO], cell-free mitochondrial DNA [cf-mtDNA]) measured pre- and post-session. Forest walking elicited higher high-frequency (HF) power, a lower LF/HF ratio, and greater increases in the SIgA/total protein ratio (p < 0.001) compared to urban walking. Furthermore, the forest condition yielded significantly greater psychological improvements and reduced negative moods, including anger (p = 0.002) and fatigue (p = 0.010). Reductions in cortisol, cf-mtDNA, and NO showed significant condition × time interaction effects. Additionally, an overnight forest stay significantly enhanced baseline SIgA and happiness while reducing stress markers. In conclusion, forest-based walking interventions elicit more favorable physiological and psychological responses than urban park walking. By enhancing parasympathetic activation, immune function, and psychological well-being, forest walking serves as a practical, evidence-based strategy to promote holistic health in postmenopausal women.

artigos.titulo: Implementation of WHO Self-Help Plus among Ukrainian university students during wartime: A multicenter longitudinal study
artigos.autores: Pinchuk I, Kaminska S, Chumak S et al.
artigos.destaque: WHO SH+ is an effective, scalable first-line psychosocial intervention for university students in wartime. It alleviates distress, enhances functioning, and maintains benefits over 3 months. SH+ can be rapidly deployed by non-specialists within stepped-care university frameworks during humanitarian crises. Flexible delivery and alignment with academic schedules are essential to overcome conflict-driven barriers.

resumo.texto: Prolonged war-related adversity places Ukrainian university students at heightened risk of psychological distress. Scalable, low-intensity interventions such as WHO Self-Help Plus (SH+) show promise, yet evidence of their implementation and short-term effectiveness during active conflict is limited.

A multicenter longitudinal study was conducted across five universities. Students with mild-to-moderate distress (PSS-10) joined a 5-week offline Acceptance and Commitment Therapy-based SH+ course led by trained non-specialist facilitators. Outcomes included psychological distress (PHQ-9, GAD-7, PCL-5), well-being (WHO-5), daily functioning (WHODAS 2.0), and resilience (CD-RISC-10), assessed at baseline (T1), post-intervention (T2), and 3-month follow-up (T3). Analyses used non-parametric longitudinal tests on 297 completers.

SH+ participation significantly reduced perceived stress, depression, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress from T1 to T2. Well-being and daily functioning improved, with all gains sustained at T3. Resilience remained stable. Implementation barriers included security threats, power outages, and exam overlaps, contributing to attrition.

WHO SH+ is an effective, scalable first-line psychosocial intervention for university students in wartime. It alleviates distress, enhances functioning, and maintains benefits over 3 months. SH+ can be rapidly deployed by non-specialists within stepped-care university frameworks during humanitarian crises. Flexible delivery and alignment with academic schedules are essential to overcome conflict-driven barriers.

artigos.titulo: A Behavioral Paradigm for Investigating Stress-Induced Anxiety-Like States In Drosophila melanogaster
artigos.autores: Alia AG, Hirano Y
artigos.destaque: Following exposure to aversive stimuli, flies display robust avoidance of the narrow arm, exhibiting a claustrophobia-like behavioral shift consistent with a sustained and generalized anxiety-like state. This assay provides a simple, scalable, and ethologically relevant approach for studying stress-induced behavioral modulation in Drosophila, expanding the toolkit available for modeling anxiety-related states.

resumo.texto: Animals exhibit behavioral changes following exposure to aversive stimuli, and these responses often generalize across contexts, providing a useful framework for investigating stress-induced and anxiety-like states. Traditional rodent assays such as the elevated plus maze, open field test, and light-dark box have been instrumental in characterizing anxiety-like behavior, yet additional complementary models are needed to capture the diversity and complexity of these states across species. Here, an assay for Drosophila melanogaster, designed to quantify stress-induced behavioral responses, was used to study the mechanisms underpinning anxiety-like states. Flies are first exposed to a strong electric shock or heat shock and subsequently tested in a two-arm choice arena offering a narrow versus a wide arm. Following exposure to aversive stimuli, flies display robust avoidance of the narrow arm, exhibiting a claustrophobia-like behavioral shift consistent with a sustained and generalized anxiety-like state. This assay provides a simple, scalable, and ethologically relevant approach for studying stress-induced behavioral modulation in Drosophila, expanding the toolkit available for modeling anxiety-related states.

artigos.titulo: Time-out with humor-an intervention project for burnout prevention in a family health unit
artigos.autores: Jácome M, Graça B, Santos AMLDS et al.
artigos.destaque: Within-group pre-post changes were not statistically significant, and no significant differences were observed in the remaining burnout domains or in well-being.ConclusionsThe intervention was associated with lower patient-related burnout. Despite limitations in sample size and study design, findings suggest potential benefits of humor-based approaches in healthcare.

resumo.texto: BackgroundBurnout syndrome, characterized by emotional exhaustion, reduced personal accomplishment, and detachment, affects personal and professional well-being. Humor-based interventions have been explored as strategies to promote psychological resilience.ObjectiveTo assess the impact of a humor-based intervention combined with team-building sessions on burnout levels among professionals in a Family Health Unit.MethodsControlled before-after study in two Family Health Units. The intervention group comprised 6 physicians, 6 nurses and 4 secretaries; the control group 5 physicians, 5 nurses and 4 secretaries. Median age was 47.5 years (IQR 19.25) in the control and 50.0 years (IQR 11.75) in the intervention group; 76.7% were female. At baseline and post-intervention, participants completed the Multidimensional Sense of Humor Scale, the Copenhagen Burnout Inventory-Portuguese version, and the Personal Wellbeing Index-Adult. Over one year, intervention group staff participated in weekly humor-viewing sessions and two psychologist-led workshops on communication skills and burnout prevention. The primary outcome was change in burnout across three domains (personal, work-related, patient-related); the secondary outcome was subjective well-being.ResultsA statistically significant between-group difference in patient-related burnout was found at post-intervention: scores increased in the control group and decreased in the intervention group (p = 0.04). Within-group pre-post changes were not statistically significant, and no significant differences were observed in the remaining burnout domains or in well-being.ConclusionsThe intervention was associated with lower patient-related burnout. Despite limitations in sample size and study design, findings suggest potential benefits of humor-based approaches in healthcare.

artigos.titulo: Cardiometabolic, Physiological and Objective-Sleep Responses to Transcendental Meditation: Secondary Analysis of a Randomised Controlled Trial Among University Staff
artigos.autores: Khanal MK, Karimi L, Saunders P et al.
artigos.destaque: TM was associated with small, non-robust diastolic BP reduction with no effect on other outcomes. Burnout may modify HRV response, but this finding requires confirmation in adequately powered trials.

resumo.texto: Chronic stress contributes to cardiometabolic risk, and stress-reduction interventions have been proposed to improve stress-sensitive physiology and cardiometabolic health, though evidence remains inconsistent. This study examined the effects of a Transcendental Meditation (TM) intervention on cardiometabolic health and upstream physiological outcomes.

This two-arm, open-label RCT compared TM (n = 65) with control (access to university well-being resource, n = 64) among Australian university staff. Secondary outcomes included blood pressure (BP), fasting glucose, HOMA insulin resistance (IR), lipids, C-reactive protein, salivary cortisol, heart rate variability (HRV), sympathetic arousal, and a post hoc composite cardiometabolic risk (CMR) score. Post hoc exploratory analyses tested whether burnout, sex and baseline metabolic risk moderated TM effects on HRV, total cholesterol, cortisol slope and IR. Primary analyses were intention-to-treat.

TM was associated with a small diastolic BP reduction (-1.18 mmHg [95% CI: -2.35, -0.01], interaction p = 0.036), with a non-significant trend in the endpoint-only analysis (p = 0.064); no other outcomes differed between groups. Burnout moderated the HRV response (p = 0.02), favouring higher-burnout participants and sex moderated the cholesterol response (p = 0.011), with TM attenuating the control-group rise in females, with uncertainty on LDL and HDL. Interactions for cortisol slope (by sex) and HOMA-IR (by metabolic risk) were non-significant; stratified comparisons suggested numerically greater improvement in TM males and higher-risk participants, respectively. Given no multiplicity correction, all findings are hypothesis-generating only.
TM was associated with small, non-robust diastolic BP reduction with no effect on other outcomes. Burnout may modify HRV response, but this finding requires confirmation in adequately powered trials.

artigos.titulo: Relationship between Profile, Quality of Life and Burden of Older People With Dementia's Caregivers during the COVID-19 Pandemic
artigos.autores: Gerassi RC, de Andrade LP, Tsen C et al.
artigos.destaque: The fewer years of study, the higher quality of life the caregiver presents. The lower caregiver quality of life, the higher caregiver distress related to behavioral symptoms, and the older people's behavioral symptoms, the higher the caregiver burden is.

resumo.texto: This study was to verify the quality of life and caregiver burden of older people with dementia during the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (COVID-19) pandemic, and the clinical and sociodemographic factors associated with them. This cross-sectional study was conducted remotely and included Brazilian older people with a mild to moderate stage of dementia and their family caregivers. The caregivers reported older people's clinical and sociodemographic characteristics. Caregiver characteristics were also collected. The sample comprised 37 pairs of older adults and caregivers, involving older adults with a mean age of 77.5 years old and caregivers who were mostly women (86.5%). Only caregiver years of study and caregiver burden significantly influenced caregiver quality of life. Caregiver distress related to older people's behavior symptoms, older people's behavioral symptoms and caregiver quality of life influenced caregiver burden. These caregivers have a fair quality of life and moderate to mild burden during the COVID-19 pandemic. The fewer years of study, the higher quality of life the caregiver presents. The lower caregiver quality of life, the higher caregiver distress related to behavioral symptoms, and the older people's behavioral symptoms, the higher the caregiver burden is.

artigos.titulo: Development of Elective Flexibility and Related Cognitive Functions Across Three Cultures
artigos.autores: Pope-Caldwell S, Felsche E, Dzabatou A et al.
artigos.destaque: Next, using interviews with 62 adults from these three cultural groups we found evidence that cultural variation in daily exposure to unpredictable variability corresponded with more elective switching whereas exposure to harshness corresponded with less. By combining richly contextualized cross-cultural and developmental data with multiple cognitive tests and computational models, this research uniquely contributes to our understanding of the development of children's flexible decision-making skillsets.

resumo.texto: Elective flexibility, the ability to switch between working strategies adaptively, is critical for decision-making in complex environments. Here we experimentally assessed elective flexibility alongside three related cognitive measures short-term memory, inhibition, and responsive flexibility-in 325 children and adults (ages 4-81-years) from three cultures. Elective flexibility performance improved with age for Germans and, to some extent, for Congolese BaYaka and Bandongo participants. Under stable conditions, younger German children were more explorative than older children and adolescents. Next, using interviews with 62 adults from these three cultural groups we found evidence that cultural variation in daily exposure to unpredictable variability corresponded with more elective switching whereas exposure to harshness corresponded with less. By combining richly contextualized cross-cultural and developmental data with multiple cognitive tests and computational models, this research uniquely contributes to our understanding of the development of children's flexible decision-making skillsets.

artigos.titulo: Large language model chatbots for patient-facing erectile dysfunction information: a cross-sectional evaluation of safety, accuracy, empathy, information quality and readability
artigos.autores: Liang D, Zhang Z, Zhao W et al.
artigos.destaque: Large language model chatbots generally provided accurate ED-related information, but performance varied across clinically relevant dimensions. They may support information seeking, but should not replace individualized clinical assessment.

resumo.texto: Generative artificial intelligence chatbots are increasingly used for health information, including sensitive conditions, such as erectile dysfunction (ED), but their safety and quality remain uncertain. To compare six large language model chatbot interfaces for ED information across safety, accuracy, empathy, information quality, source-related transparency, readability and response length.

Thirty-eight standardized ED questions were submitted once to six chatbot interfaces, yielding 228 responses. Five independent raters assessed Safety, Accuracy, Empathy, DISCERN, Ensuring Quality Information for Patients, the Journal of the American Medical Association benchmark and Global Quality Score. Readability and response length were also evaluated. Between-interface differences were tested using Cochran's Q or Friedman tests.

Twenty-six responses (11.4%) were safety-flagged. Safety-flag frequency differed across interfaces (Q = 11.765, P = 0.038), but the effect size was small (0.062; 95% CI, 0.026-0.148), and no pairwise difference remained significant after multiplicity correction. Accuracy was generally high (median 4.00/5 for all interfaces), but differed slightly overall (P = 0.010, Kendall's W = 0.080). Empathy (P < 0.001, W = 0.160), DISCERN (P = 0.003, W = 0.508), Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (P < 0.001, W = 0.576), and Journal of the American Medical Association benchmark scores (P < 0.001, W = 0.888) differed significantly, whereas Global Quality Score did not (P = 0.146). Readability and response length also differed (all P < 0.001).

Large language model chatbots generally provided accurate ED-related information, but performance varied across clinically relevant dimensions. They may support information seeking, but should not replace individualized clinical assessment.

artigos.titulo: Quality, Readability, and Reliability of Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Responses to Parent-Centered Questions on Newborn Hearing Screening: A Cross-Sectional Comparative Study
artigos.autores: Ozses A, Yilmaz BD, Ozses M
artigos.destaque: LLM-based chatbots generally perform acceptably on newborn hearing screening questions, although substantial variability was observed across models. Despite acceptable readability levels, chatbot-generated content remains relatively difficult to read. LLMs may serve as complementary information resources for parents seeking information about newborn hearing screening, although further research is needed before their routine clinical use.

resumo.texto: Parents increasingly use large language models (LLMs) to obtain health-related information; however, the quality, readability, and reliability of AI-generated patient education remain uncertain. This study evaluated the performance of three LLM-based chatbots in providing parent-centred information regarding newborn hearing screening.

Thirty-eight parent-centred questions regarding newborn hearing screening were submitted to ChatGPT-5.1, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and DeepSeek-V3. Responses were assessed using a five-point Likert scale for accuracy, comprehensiveness, clarity, and credibility. Responses were assessed using the modified EQIP for quality, and the Flesch Reading Ease Score (FRES) and Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL) for readability.

DeepSeek-V3 outperformed both ChatGPT-5.1 and Gemini 2.5 Flash in accuracy and comprehensiveness (p < 0.05), whereas its clarity scores were lower (p < 0.05). The FRES scores (51.5-59.3) indicated difficult readability, whereas the FKGL scores (8.4-8.9) corresponded to an eighth-grade reading level. Gemini 2.5 Flash demonstrated higher FRES scores (p = 0.001). mEQIP scores were not significant (p = 0.148) and indicated good quality.

LLM-based chatbots generally perform acceptably on newborn hearing screening questions, although substantial variability was observed across models. Despite acceptable readability levels, chatbot-generated content remains relatively difficult to read. LLMs may serve as complementary information resources for parents seeking information about newborn hearing screening, although further research is needed before their routine clinical use.

This study addresses the JECP journal's aim to evaluate the clinical applications of emerging artificial intelligence technologies in healthcare. Evaluating the quality, accuracy, readability, and reliability of chatbot-generated information for newborn hearing screening provides evidence to support person-centred care, patient education, and the responsible integration of AI into clinical practice.

artigos.titulo: Clinical Reasoning During Acute Decompensation: A Metacognitive Act
artigos.autores: Bache AJ, Durning SJ, Merkebu J
artigos.destaque: Transitioning from diagnosis to action requires dynamic cognitive flexibility with clinical reasoning. Recognizing missed opportunities post-hoc represents a substantive finding for reflective learning, though it does not imply identical awareness was active during the event. Educational strategies must separately address real-time cognitive pivoting during crisis and post-event debriefing.

resumo.texto: Medical errors contribute to preventable morbidity and mortality. Categories of error include diagnostic and management error, to which lack of urgency, understanding, or awareness contribute. While physician reasoning is influenced by medical content, acute clinical situations require rapid metacognitive shifts-moving from diagnostic hypothesis generation to decisive management action. This study investigated physician clinical reasoning and how it is impacted by emotion and metacognitive reflection during this critical transition from diagnosis to procedural intervention in an acute inpatient encounter.

Physicians (n = 19) diagnosed and managed a live simulation of acute patient decompensation. Clinical reasoning performance was assessed with clinical benchmarks and utilizing a novel video-stimulated think-aloud protocol immediately following the encounter; participants reflected aloud while reviewing their recorded performance. Verbatim transcripts were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis, informed by situated cognition and SchÖn's reflective framework.

Themes of deliberation, prioritization and fixation, and reflection were identified. Effective clinical reasoning depended on executing timely metacognitive shifts to bridge the gap between diagnostic recognition and management action. Video recall revealed distinctions between real-time cognitive processing (reflection-in-action) and post-hoc insights (reflection-on-action). Environmental cues, such as nurse prompting, functioned as distributed cognitive support. Notably, emotional distress often coexisted with effective prioritization, while procedural hesitation stemmed from both metacognitive regulation and limited procedural familiarity.

Transitioning from diagnosis to action requires dynamic cognitive flexibility with clinical reasoning. Recognizing missed opportunities post-hoc represents a substantive finding for reflective learning, though it does not imply identical awareness was active during the event. Educational strategies must separately address real-time cognitive pivoting during crisis and post-event debriefing.

artigos.titulo: Kids who eat more ultra-processed foods show a troubling brain response
artigos.destaque: A new study suggests that ultra-processed foods may influence children's developing brains in ways that encourage weight gain. Researchers from USC studied 46 children ages 7 to 10 and found that those who ate more ultra-processed foods showed stronger activity in the brain's reward system when viewing tempting foods like cookies and French fries. These heightened brain responses were linked to greater increases in body fat and body mass index (BMI) one year later, suggesting that the brain's sensitivity to food cues may help explain why ultra-processed diets are associated with obesity.

artigos.titulo: The brain’s hidden fear mechanism may explain anxiety and PTSD
artigos.destaque: A surprising new discovery suggests that fear may cause the brain to blur the line between danger and safety rather than distinguish them more clearly. By observing brain activity in mice using augmented reality, scientists found that memories of threatening and harmless environments began to overlap, potentially allowing faster responses to danger. This "better safe than sorry" survival mechanism could help explain why people with anxiety or PTSD sometimes experience intense fear in completely safe situations.

artigos.titulo: Digital Augmentation of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 for Obesity Management: Retrospective Study
artigos.autores: Davey B, Dabash O, Khanna R et al.
artigos.destaque: Augmenting GLP-1 RA treatment with a behavioral smartphone app was associated with a higher likelihood of achieving clinically significant weight loss, although differences in overall weight-loss trajectories were modest. Progress logging emerged as the primary behavioral predictor of improved outcomes. While not causal effects, these findings are consistent with the positive value of integrating digital tools with pharmacotherapy for weight loss.

resumo.texto: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), including semaglutide and tirzepatide, are highly effective for weight management; however, long-term outcomes depend on sustained behavioral engagement. Digital health tools may enhance these behavioral components, but evidence regarding their real-world benefit alongside pharmacotherapy remains limited.

This study aims to evaluate whether augmenting a direct-to-consumer GLP-1 RA program with a behavioral support smartphone app improves weight-loss outcomes compared with medication alone, and to identify which app features are associated with weight loss over time.

A retrospective observational cohort study was conducted using data from 6113 adults (older than 18 years) in Australia who self-enrolled into the Mosh direct-to-consumer weight-loss program between July 1, 2024, and August 13, 2025, with their weight data recorded at baseline and at least 1 other timepoint. Participants received semaglutide or tirzepatide, with optional access to a smartphone app and clinician support. Logistic regression models examined achievement of ≥5%, ≥10%, and ≥15% weight-loss thresholds at 60, 120, and 180 days. Linear mixed-effects models interacting with app feature use, with linear and quadratic time terms, assessed the association of different features with percentage weight loss trajectories over time. Both models adjusted for medication type, gender, ethnicity, age, and baseline BMI.

Participants using the program plus medication had higher odds of achieving clinically significant weight loss than those using medication only. Adjusted odds ratio point estimates for day 60, 120, and 180 (±10) days indicated they were 1.38 (95% CI 1.09-1.75) times to 2.22 (95% CI 1.40-3.45) times more likely to achieve ≥5% weight loss across timepoints, 1.67 (95% CI 1.33-2.10) times to 1.97 (95% CI 1.35-2.90) times more likely to achieve ≥10% weight loss by day 120 and 180, and 1.99 (95% CI 1.26-3.29) times more likely to achieve ≥15% weight loss by 180 days. Mixed-effects modeling demonstrated that progress logging was associated with more rapid weight loss over time (β=.26 percentage-point additional weight lost per 30 days, SE 0.06; t4336=4.46; 95% CI 0.14-0.38; P<.001). No other app features were consistently associated with changes in weight-loss trajectories.

Augmenting GLP-1 RA treatment with a behavioral smartphone app was associated with a higher likelihood of achieving clinically significant weight loss, although differences in overall weight-loss trajectories were modest. Progress logging emerged as the primary behavioral predictor of improved outcomes. While not causal effects, these findings are consistent with the positive value of integrating digital tools with pharmacotherapy for weight loss.

artigos.titulo: Pilot Implementation of an Adapted Online Clinic-Community Model for Childhood Obesity
artigos.autores: Chew CSE, Khaider KB, Neshteruk CD et al.
artigos.destaque: The adapted online model was feasible and acceptable, with preliminary improvements in physical quality of life, movement skills, and BMI metrics. Larger adequately powered trials are needed to confirm effectiveness and longer-term outcomes.

resumo.texto: Intensive health-behaviour lifestyle treatment is recommended for paediatric obesity, but evidence for young children and synchronous online delivery remains limited.
To evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary effectiveness of an adapted online clinic-community model for children aged 4 to < 8 years with overweight or obesity.

In this two-arm randomized controlled trial, children were randomized to an online family-based intervention or usual care. The primary outcome was treatment dose at 6 months, defined as intervention contact hours. Secondary outcomes included BMI z-score, percentage of the 95th BMI percentile, health-related quality of life, eating behaviours, and perceived movement skills at 3 and 6 months.

Forty children were enrolled; mean age was 6.6 ± 1.0 years and 58% were male. At 6 months, 70% of intervention participants achieved at least 26 treatment hours. Although the between-group differences were not statistically significant, the intervention group demonstrated numerically greater reductions in BMI z-score (-0.2 ± 0.3 vs. -0.1 ± 0.1; p = 0.091) and percentage of the 95th BMI percentile (-3.5 ± 6.4 vs. -0.2 ± 4.0; p = 0.075). Physical quality of life improved at 3 and 6 months, object control skills at 3 months, and perceived locomotor skills at 6 months.

The adapted online model was feasible and acceptable, with preliminary improvements in physical quality of life, movement skills, and BMI metrics. Larger adequately powered trials are needed to confirm effectiveness and longer-term outcomes.

artigos.titulo: Cardiovascular and diabetes outcomes after metabolic bariatric surgery versus obesity management medications: nationwide overlap-weighted cohort study of 379 858 patients
artigos.autores: Gillikin AP, Rabinovich EP, Nimeri AA et al.
artigos.destaque: Among adults with obesity and T2D, MBS was associated with greater %TWL, higher glycaemic normalization, and lower 5-year risks of nephropathy, retinopathy, MACE, and all-cause mortality compared with real-world initiation of OMMs among patients in clinical equipoise, supporting the role of MBS as a durable therapy in multimodal obesity management.

resumo.texto: Metabolic bariatric surgery (MBS) and incretin-based therapy (IBT) are effective treatments for obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, their comparative effectiveness in current practice remains incompletely defined.

Adults aged ≥18 years with obesity and T2D who underwent MBS or initiated obesity management medications (OMMs) were identified. The median follow-up was 4.9 (interquartile range (i.q.r.) 3.6-6.7) years for MBS and 4.3 (i.q.r. 3.4-5.8) years for IBT. Overlap weighting balanced baseline covariates between groups. Five-year outcomes included nephropathy, retinopathy, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and all-cause mortality. One-year outcomes included percentage total weight loss (%TWL) and rates of haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) <6.5%.

In total, 379 858 adults met the inclusion criteria (32 401 underwent MBS and 347 457 initiated OMMs). After overlap weighting, baseline covariates were well balanced. Compared with OMMs, MBS was associated with lower 5-year cumulative incidences of nephropathy (4.5% versus 8.3%; -3.8% points; HR 0.55 (95% c.i. 0.52 to 0.60)), retinopathy (3.6% versus 7.4%; -3.8% points; HR 0.60 (95% c.i. 0.55 to 0.65)), MACE (6.1% versus 8.1%; -2.0% points; HR 0.78 (95% c.i. 0.73 to 0.84)), and all-cause mortality (2.1% versus 3.7%; -1.6% points; HR 0.61 (95% c.i. 0.55 to 0.69)). At 1 year, the mean %TWL was greater after MBS (25.4% (95% c.i. 25.3% to 25.5%)) than after OMMs (6.4% (95% c.i. 6.3% to 6.5%)). Among patients with baseline HbA1c ≥6.5%, the proportion achieving HbA1c <6.5% at 1 year was higher after MBS (76.7% (95% c.i. 75.3% to 78.0%)) than after OMMs (47.2% (95% c.i. 46.2% to 48.1%); P < 0.001). Findings were consistent across agent-stratified, competing-risk, landmark, and no-censoring sensitivity analyses.

Among adults with obesity and T2D, MBS was associated with greater %TWL, higher glycaemic normalization, and lower 5-year risks of nephropathy, retinopathy, MACE, and all-cause mortality compared with real-world initiation of OMMs among patients in clinical equipoise, supporting the role of MBS as a durable therapy in multimodal obesity management.

artigos.titulo: Medium- and long-chain triacylglycerols regulate glucose, lipid metabolism and liver metabolomics under different protein levels in aged male C57BL/6J mice
artigos.autores: Cheng X, Jiang C, Wei W et al.
artigos.destaque: Hepatic metabolomic analysis further revealed that MLCT markedly reshaped metabolic pathways associated with lipid oxidation, carbohydrate metabolism, amino acid metabolism, and insulin-related signaling pathways. Overall, these findings indicate that MLCT exerts protein-dependent metabolic benefits in aged mice by improving hepatic glucose-lipid metabolic coordination and systemic metabolic homeostasis, providing mechanistic support for precision lipid-based nutritional strategies in aging populations.

resumo.texto: Medium- and long-chain triacylglycerols (MLCT) have been shown to exert beneficial effects on sarcopenia in 16-month-old male C57BL/6J aged mice. However, the underlying mechanism of how MLCT regulates lipid metabolism to confer these beneficial effects remains to be elucidated. In this study, 16-month-old male C57BL/6J mice were fed diets containing long-chain triacylglycerols (LCT), a physical blend of medium-chain and long-chain triacylglycerols (MCT/LCT), or MLCT under low-, medium-, or high-protein levels for 12 weeks. Under low- and medium-protein levels, the MLCT intervention was more effective at reducing serum glucose levels, increasing HDL-C/LDL-C ratio, improving liver function indicators, and decreasing hepatic lipid accumulation in aged mice than the LCT and MCT/LCT interventions. Both MLCT and MCT/LCT significantly increased serum ketone body levels, with MLCT demonstrating a moderate ketogenic effect. In contrast, under the high-protein level, the serum glucose and lipid metabolic differences among the three structured lipids were markedly attenuated. Compared with LCT and MCT/LCT groups, MLCT intervention significantly decreased serum IL-1, IL-6, and TNF-α levels by 43.47% and 25.36%, 13.98%% and 10.60%, 33.77% and 1.89%, respectively. Hepatic metabolomic analysis further revealed that MLCT markedly reshaped metabolic pathways associated with lipid oxidation, carbohydrate metabolism, amino acid metabolism, and insulin-related signaling pathways. Overall, these findings indicate that MLCT exerts protein-dependent metabolic benefits in aged mice by improving hepatic glucose-lipid metabolic coordination and systemic metabolic homeostasis, providing mechanistic support for precision lipid-based nutritional strategies in aging populations.

artigos.titulo: Evidence for spermine oxidase (SMOX) as a regulator of skeletal muscle mass throughout the lifespan
artigos.autores: Montenegro CF, Murach KA, Chambers TL
artigos.destaque: In humans, higher basal SMOX expression after strength training correlates to higher strength gains, but investigations of SMOX's actions in humans are lacking. Further defining the role of SMOX in animal and human models will facilitate future skeletal muscle-specific therapeutics to promote youthfulness during ageing.

resumo.texto: Age-associated loss of muscle mass and function, termed sarcopenia, increases morbidity and mortality risks concomitant with decreased physical activity. Chronic exercise training is the most effective countermeasure against sarcopenia, but physical limitations create a barrier to participation in the elderly. Investigation into alternative pharmaceutical and nutraceutical treatments to prevent sarcopenia and maintain muscle plasticity late-in-life are therefore warranted. Polyamine metabolism regulates many facets of skeletal muscle biology with the potential for targeted treatments in conditions of compromised muscle health and plasticity. Particularly, spermidine is shown to benefit muscle health in mammalian models of ageing and exercise training. Endogenous production of spermidine is partially regulated by the enzyme spermine oxidase (SMOX). SMOX catabolism cleaves spermine into spermidine to maintain a healthy polyamine pool. Anabolic signaling regulates SMOX expression suggesting a supporting role of polyamines during muscle hypertrophy. SMOX overexpression in skeletal muscle retains muscle fiber size in atrophy-inducing animal models (e.g. immobilization, fasting, denervation) potentially driven by reciprocal downregulation of p21, a marker of cellular senescence. In satellite cells, spermidine improves satellite cell function by restoring autophagy and mitophagy, potentially related to anti-ageing Yamanaka factors. Abundance of SMOX is highest in fast-twitch muscle fiber types but can respond in a fiber-type and exercise dependent manner. In humans, higher basal SMOX expression after strength training correlates to higher strength gains, but investigations of SMOX's actions in humans are lacking. Further defining the role of SMOX in animal and human models will facilitate future skeletal muscle-specific therapeutics to promote youthfulness during ageing.

artigos.titulo: Impact of sarcopenia on clinical outcomes after endoscopic and endovascular interventions for bleeding gastric varices: A multi-center real-world study
artigos.autores: Biswas S, Mitra S, Kumar SE et al.
artigos.destaque: The presence of sarcopenia is a risk factor for further decompensation and mortality after GV hemorrhage in cirrhosis.

resumo.texto: The impact of sarcopenia on the clinical outcomes following gastric variceal (GV) hemorrhage in cirrhosis remains unclear.

We retrospectively analyzed patients with cirrhosis and GV bleeding from six centers in India (January 2017-January 2023). Baseline demographics, further decompensation events-rebleeding, ascites and hepatic encephalopathy (HE) and mortality-were reviewed. Cross-sectional imaging was used to assess skeletal muscle index (SMI). Sarcopenia was defined using gender-specific SMI thresholds (men, < 42 cm2/m2 and women, < 38 cm2/m2). Competing risk analysis was used to evaluate predictors of rebleeding and further decompensation with mortality as a competing event.

Total 318 patients (214 males, 67.3%) were included. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (49/79, 62%) was the leading cause for cirrhosis in patients with sarcopenia. Sarcopenia was associated with higher risk of rebleeding (sHR, 1.62, 95% CI, 1.03-2.52; p = 0.03), further decompensation (sHR, 2.02, 95% CI, 1.43-2.85; p < 0.001) and a one, two and three-year probability of mortality of 15.3%, 24.9% and 41.1% as compared to 9.1%, 14.9% and 14.9% in non-sarcopenic patients. On multi-variate analysis, sarcopenia was an independent predictor of both further decompensation (sHR, 2.03, 95% CI, 1.39-2.97; p < 0.01) and mortality (HR, 1.98, 95% CI, 1.11-3.54; p = 0.020).
The presence of sarcopenia is a risk factor for further decompensation and mortality after GV hemorrhage in cirrhosis.

artigos.titulo: Prognostic value of the red blood cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio in alcohol-related sarcopenia
artigos.autores: Domínguez-González V, Ribot-Hernández I, García-Rodríguez A et al.
artigos.destaque: The predictive capacity of RAR was high (AUC 0.81; 95% CI 0.67-0.94). In conclusion, RAR is a simple, low-cost, and independent prognostic biomarker that integrates inflammatory and nutritional status in patients with alcohol use disorder and sarcopenia.

resumo.texto: Chronic alcohol consumption is associated with sarcopenia, a metabolic disorder characterized by progressive loss of muscle mass and function. The red blood cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) has emerged as a composite biomarker reflecting inflammation, oxidative stress, and nutritional status. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of RAR in patients with alcohol use disorder and sarcopenia. We conducted a prospective observational study including 231 patients with chronic alcohol consumption (mean intake 200 g/day) recruited at a tertiary hospital between 2008 and 2025. Clinical, analytical, and body composition variables were assessed using densitometry and handgrip strength. Probable sarcopenia was defined according to EWGSOP2 criteria based on low muscle strength. Cox and logistic regression models and ROC curve analysis were performed. RAR was positively associated with liver dysfunction and inflammatory markers, and inversely correlated with appendicular lean mass and handgrip strength. In patients with probable sarcopenia, RAR was independently associated with 12-month mortality (hazard ratio 1.67; 95% confidence interval 1.32-2.11; p < 0.001). The predictive capacity of RAR was high (AUC 0.81; 95% CI 0.67-0.94). In conclusion, RAR is a simple, low-cost, and independent prognostic biomarker that integrates inflammatory and nutritional status in patients with alcohol use disorder and sarcopenia.

artigos.titulo: Revitalizing aging muscles: harnessing NAD⁺, sirtuins, and exercise to combat sarcopenia
artigos.autores: Wang Y, Zhang G
artigos.destaque: We conclude that pharmacological NAD⁺ restoration alone is currently insufficient to reverse sarcopenia in humans. A synergistic approach combining exercise with targeted NAD⁺ support, together with emerging strategies involving precursor transporters, trigonelline and hypothalamic NAD⁺-sirtuin circuits, represents a testable avenue that requires rigorous, stratified clinical evaluation.

resumo.texto: Aging is associated with systemic metabolic dysfunction that contributes to geriatric syndromes such as sarcopenia-the progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass and function. Evidence from preclinical models suggests that age-associated depletion of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD⁺) may contribute to this decline by limiting the activity of sirtuin deacetylases (SIRT1-7). These enzymes act as metabolic sensors regulating mitochondrial biogenesis, oxidative capacity, DNA repair and pathways related to muscle atrophy. Physical exercise enhances NAD⁺ salvage through upregulation of nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT). Pharmacological approaches including NAD⁺ precursor supplementation (nicotinamide riboside or nicotinamide mononucleotide) and inhibition of NAD⁺-consuming enzymes have shown benefits in preclinical models. However, clinical translation remains inconsistent. Recent meta-analyses have found no significant effect of these precursors on muscle mass or strength in adults aged over 60 years. Moreover, experimental evidence indicates that even profound NAD⁺ depletion in adult mouse skeletal muscle does not necessarily compromise function or accelerate aging. We conclude that pharmacological NAD⁺ restoration alone is currently insufficient to reverse sarcopenia in humans. A synergistic approach combining exercise with targeted NAD⁺ support, together with emerging strategies involving precursor transporters, trigonelline and hypothalamic NAD⁺-sirtuin circuits, represents a testable avenue that requires rigorous, stratified clinical evaluation.

artigos.titulo: Osteosarcopenia as a Systems-Level Failure of the Bone-Muscle Functional Unit
artigos.autores: Dai H, Liu J, Zang W et al.
artigos.destaque: Mechanistic claims in this review are primarily supported by preclinical evidence; human causal evidence remains incomplete. Full statement in Online Resource 1.

resumo.texto: Osteosarcopenia-osteoporosis co-occurring with sarcopenia-has a pooled prevalence of 18.5% in older adults (range 5-37%) and carries increased risks of fracture (HR 2.13, 95% CI 1.61-2.81), falls (HR 1.54, 95% CI 1.20-1.97), and mortality (HR 1.75, 95% CI 1.34-2.28). Often framed as simple coexistence, osteosarcopenia is proposed as a systems-level disorder of interconnected bone-muscle degeneration.

We synthesize evidence from molecular biology, systems physiology, and translational research showing that osteosarcopenia is a systems-level failure of the bone-muscle functional unit, a highly integrated structure maintained by bidirectional mechanical coupling, osteokine-myokine exchange, and shared intracellular signaling pathways. We examine how intrinsic aging mechanisms (genomic and epigenetic drift, transcriptional reprogramming, structural co-degeneration, and metabolic-mechanical decoupling) and systemic drivers (inflammaging, adipose dysfunction, gut dysbiosis, and hormonal decline) converge to reconfigure this crosstalk from a homeostatic regulator into a pathological amplifier. At the center of this process is a vicious cycle of declining osteocalcin and irisin alongside rising sclerostin, FGF23, and myostatin, propagated through shared signaling hubs (Wnt/β-catenin, TGF-β/Smad, IGF-1/Akt/FOXO, and NF-κB) and sustained by gut-bone-muscle axes. We advance this systems-level framing as an integrative hypothesis rather than established fact: more-than-additive risk and synergistic treatment effects are not yet demonstrated in humans. Actionable now are dual-tissue screening, guideline-based treatment of each component, and combined exercise and nutritional strategies; biomarker-guided care and crosstalk-targeted pharmacology await prospective validation.
Mechanistic claims in this review are primarily supported by preclinical evidence; human causal evidence remains incomplete. Full statement in Online Resource 1.

artigos.titulo: Menopause, Weight Loss, and Pelvic Floor Changes: Clinical and Aesthetic Considerations
artigos.autores: Chirumamilla V, Tyler KH
artigos.destaque: Dermatologists should recognize functional symptoms, provide evidence-based counseling, and coordinate care with gynecology, urogynecology, urology, and pelvic floor physical therapy while approaching emerging procedural therapies cautiously.

resumo.texto: Menopause is associated with hormonal, structural, and functional changes affecting the vulvovaginal tissues, pelvic floor, and urinary tract. Weight loss may further alter soft-tissue volume and body composition, although effects on pelvic floor function remain incompletely understood.

The aim of this study was to review menopause-associated vulvovaginal and pelvic floor changes and discuss implications for dermatologic evaluation, weight loss, symptom management, and procedural counseling.

A narrative review of literature addressing menopause, pelvic floor dysfunction, weight loss, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, pelvic floor rehabilitation, and emerging vulvovaginal therapies was performed.

Menopause-associated tissue remodeling may contribute to genitourinary syndrome of menopause, urinary symptoms, sexual dysfunction, and pelvic floor disorders. Weight loss may improve obesity-associated urinary incontinence but can also reduce lean mass and external soft-tissue volume. Evidence regarding glucagon-like peptide-1 therapies and pelvic floor function remains limited. Pelvic floor physical therapy is an established treatment, whereas high-intensity focused electromagnetic therapy shows preliminary evidence of benefit.

Dermatologists should recognize functional symptoms, provide evidence-based counseling, and coordinate care with gynecology, urogynecology, urology, and pelvic floor physical therapy while approaching emerging procedural therapies cautiously.

artigos.titulo: Possible sarcopenia, abdominal obesity, and all-cause mortality in middle-aged and older adults with chronic kidney disease: a dual-cohort study
artigos.autores: Fu M, Wang Y, Chen S et al.
artigos.destaque: Possible sarcopenia independently predicts all-cause mortality in CKD, though this association did not retain statistical significance in CHARLS when restricted to participants with eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2. Waist circumference provides no incremental prognostic value beyond handgrip strength, and the study was underpowered to characterize the concurrent phenotype. Prognostic evaluation in CKD should focus on routine muscle strength assessment rather than abdominal adiposity.

resumo.texto: Possible sarcopenia (low muscle strength) is a strong predictor of mortality in chronic kidney disease (CKD). While abdominal obesity is prevalent, whether it predicts mortality or modifies the association between muscle weakness and mortality remains controversial. We investigated their independent and joint associations with all-cause mortality in CKD.

This study analyzed adults with CKD aged ≥45 years from CHARLS (n = 1005) and NHANES (n = 1070). Participants were categorized into four phenotypes: NPS/NAO (neither condition), NPS/AO (abdominal obesity alone), PS/NAO (possible sarcopenia alone), and PS/AO (both conditions). Mortality risk was evaluated using multivariable Cox models and restricted cubic splines.

PS/NAO was associated with elevated all-cause mortality (adjusted HR in CHARLS: 1.980, 95% CI 1.333-2.941; NHANES: 2.191, 1.194-4.020). The estimate for PS/AO was less precise and did not reach statistical significance (CHARLS: 1.288, 0.711-2.333; NHANES: 1.171, 0.661-2.075). Direct comparisons and interaction analyses revealed no evidence that abdominal obesity modified the mortality risk associated with possible sarcopenia. No significant association was observed between NPS/AO and mortality. Handgrip strength showed an inverse linear association with mortality, whereas waist circumference provided neither independent nor incremental prognostic value.

Possible sarcopenia independently predicts all-cause mortality in CKD, though this association did not retain statistical significance in CHARLS when restricted to participants with eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2. Waist circumference provides no incremental prognostic value beyond handgrip strength, and the study was underpowered to characterize the concurrent phenotype. Prognostic evaluation in CKD should focus on routine muscle strength assessment rather than abdominal adiposity.
not applicable.

artigos.titulo: Effect of Exercise Interventions on Sarcopenia-Related Outcomes in Older Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
artigos.autores: Jafari Harandi A, Tayebi SM, Tartibian B et al.
artigos.destaque: In older adults with T2DM, structured exercise training yields meaningful gains in muscle strength, physical performance, and glycemic control despite only modest effects on lean mass. These findings support resistance-based or multicomponent programs as a core component of care to address both sarcopenia-related impairments and metabolic abnormalities in this high-risk population.

resumo.texto: To systematically evaluate the effects of exercise interventions on sarcopenia-related outcomes and glycemic control in older adults with type 2 diabetes (T2DM).

We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL (January 2020-October 2025) for RCTs in adults with T2DM (mean age ≥ 65 years) comparing structured exercise (≥ 4 weeks) with nonexercise control. Co-primary outcomes were lean/appendicular lean mass, muscle strength, and physical performance; secondary outcomes were HbA1c, FPG, and HOMA-IR. Random-effects meta-analyses used Hedges' g for sarcopenia outcomes and mean differences for metabolic outcomes from pre-post changes.

Eleven RCTs (≈740 participants) were included. Exercise produced a small, nonsignificant effect on lean mass (6 trials; g = 0.14, 95% CI -0.09 to 0.37; I2 = 0%). Significant moderate-to-large improvements were found in muscle strength (nine trials; g = 0.67, 95% CI 0.46-0.88; I2 = 11.7%) and physical performance (nine trials; g = 0.74, 95% CI 0.44-1.03; I2 = 64.4%). HbA1c was reduced by 0.32 percentage points (seven trials; I2 = 0%), HOMA-IR improved by 0.51 units (three trials; I2 = 0%), while FPG changes were small and nonsignificant. Adverse events were rare and no serious exercise-related complications occurred.

In older adults with T2DM, structured exercise training yields meaningful gains in muscle strength, physical performance, and glycemic control despite only modest effects on lean mass. These findings support resistance-based or multicomponent programs as a core component of care to address both sarcopenia-related impairments and metabolic abnormalities in this high-risk population.

artigos.titulo: Discordance Between Height- and BMI-Adjusted AWGS 2025 Definitions of Confirmed Sarcopenia After Stroke
artigos.autores: Yoshimura Y, Matsumoto A, Yoneda K et al.
artigos.destaque: Height- and BMI-adjusted AWGS 2025 criteria classified approximately one in five patients differently after stroke. Beyond expected body-size differences, discordant groups exhibited distinct clinical characteristics, highlighting the importance of considering the indexing method when interpreting sarcopenia classifications.

resumo.texto: The Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) 2025 allows height- or body mass index (BMI)-adjusted muscle mass in diagnosing confirmed sarcopenia. We evaluated classification discordance and associated clinical characteristics after stroke.

This retrospective study included 864 patients undergoing post-acute stroke rehabilitation. Confirmed sarcopenia was defined using low handgrip strength combined with either height- or BMI-adjusted muscle mass. Patients were classified into four groups: Neither, Height-only, BMI-only, and Both. Agreement between definitions was quantified, and the two discordant groups were compared using multivariable logistic regression. Model robustness and discharge outcomes were examined in sensitivity and exploratory analyses, respectively.

Discordant classification occurred in 183 patients (21.2%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 18.6%-24.0%), with moderate agreement between definitions (κ = 0.578). Compared with the Height-only group, the BMI-only group had higher BMI, serum albumin, and phase angle. In adjusted analyses of 182 patients, higher albumin (odds ratio [OR] per 0.5 g/dL, 1.71; 95% CI, 1.10-2.64), phase angle (OR per degree, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.23-3.04), and medication count (OR per drug, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.03-1.32) were associated with BMI-only classification. Firth estimates were similar, but internal validation indicated overfitting. Adjusted discharge outcomes did not clearly differ between discordant groups.

Height- and BMI-adjusted AWGS 2025 criteria classified approximately one in five patients differently after stroke. Beyond expected body-size differences, discordant groups exhibited distinct clinical characteristics, highlighting the importance of considering the indexing method when interpreting sarcopenia classifications.

artigos.titulo: Semaglutide, Tirzepatide and Clinically Recorded Alcohol-Related Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Target Trial Emulation
artigos.autores: Tang H, Zhang B, Lu Y et al.
artigos.destaque: In adults with T2D, semaglutide and tirzepatide were associated with lower rates of clinically recorded AUD-related outcomes than SGLT2i, with no difference between the two GLP-1RA medications.

resumo.texto: To compare the risk of incident alcohol use disorder (AUD) among adults with Type 2 diabetes (T2D) initiating semaglutide, tirzepatide or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i).

We conducted a target trial emulation using de-identified electronic health record data from the TriNetX research network (June 2022-January 2025). Adults with T2D newly initiating semaglutide, tirzepatide or an SGLT2i were included. The primary outcome was clinically recorded hospitalization or emergency department (ED) visits for AUD. Cox proportional hazards models with 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses as well as secondary outcomes assessed the robustness of the findings.

During a mean follow-up of 0.81-1.02 years, the incidence rates (IRs) of clinically recorded hospitalization or ED visits for AUD were 2.42 versus 4.53 per 1000 person-years for semaglutide versus SGLT2i, with an HR of 0.54 (95% CI, 0.45-0.64). Similarly, the IRs were 2.34 versus 3.98 per 1000 person-years for tirzepatide versus SGLT2i, with an HR of 0.61 (95% CI, 0.46-0.83). In the direct comparison of semaglutide versus tirzepatide, IRs were 2.43 and 2.36 per 1000 person-years, respectively, with no difference in risk (HR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.73-1.31). Results were consistent across sensitivity and subgroup analyses and secondary outcomes.
In adults with T2D, semaglutide and tirzepatide were associated with lower rates of clinically recorded AUD-related outcomes than SGLT2i, with no difference between the two GLP-1RA medications.

artigos.titulo: Discovery, optimization, and Phase 1 evaluation of a novel, orally available GLP-1R/GIPR dual agonist
artigos.autores: Mowery SA, Knerr PJ, Hjøllund KR et al.
artigos.destaque: The modest weight lowering efficacy of orally administered NNC0130 highlights the continued challenges of low oral bioavailability of acylated peptides. However, the substantial efficacy observed with subcutaneous administration motivated advancement into Phase 2 clinical development.

resumo.texto: The efficacy and convenience of anti-diabetic and anti-obesity therapeutics have surged in recent years due to the emergence of incretin-based poly-pharmacological approaches as well as advances in the oral delivery of peptide drugs. We sought to combine both strategies in an orally deliverable dual agonist of the GLP-1 and GIP receptors.

We designed a panel of unimolecular, fatty-acylated peptide dual agonists, which was screened for receptor potencies in cell-based assay systems. NNC0130 was selected to advance into clinical studies using both oral and subcutaneous administration.

NNC0130 exhibited in vitro potency comparable to semaglutide at human GLP-1R and to tirzepatide at human GIPR, with a chemical structure compatible with semi-recombinant production. Its human half-life of 76-89 hours was deemed suitable for once-daily oral administration. In a multiple-ascending dose trial in participants with overweight or obesity and with separate subcutaneous and oral cohorts, daily subcutaneous administration of NNC0130 escalating from 0.3 to 3.0 mg per dose provided a placebo-corrected mean body weight loss of 9% after 12 weeks of treatment and 12% after 15 weeks. Daily oral administration escalating from 5 to 50 mg per dose provided a placebo-corrected mean body weight loss of 4% after 12 weeks, which was not statistically significantly different from zero. The relative oral bioavailability when co-formulated with permeation enhancer salcaprozate sodium was estimated to 1.6-2.2% versus s.c. administration.

The modest weight lowering efficacy of orally administered NNC0130 highlights the continued challenges of low oral bioavailability of acylated peptides. However, the substantial efficacy observed with subcutaneous administration motivated advancement into Phase 2 clinical development.

artigos.titulo: Cardiometabolic benefits of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual agonists: from obesity and diabetes to heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
artigos.autores: Chotalia R, Ghias O, Shah MU et al.
artigos.destaque: Benefits are likely mediated through weight loss dependent and weight-loss independent mechanisms. Important uncertainties remain regarding their role in non-obese HFpEF, optimal patient selection, and their safety in HFrEF.

resumo.texto: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for over half of all heart failure hospitalisations and is increasing in prevalence, largely driven by obesity and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM). Glucagon-like-peptide receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and the dual GLP-1/GIP agonist, tirzepatide, have been shown to be safe and effective medications in the treatment of T2DM and obesity as well as in obesity-related HFpEF.

This review summarises the pathophysiology of obesity-related HFpEF, mechanisms by which GLP-1 RAs and tirzepatide may improve symptoms and outcomes, and summarise evidence from recent randomised controlled and observational trials across the disease spectrum they have been studied in. Therapeutic implications and future research directions are also discussed. A structured literature search was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) up to August 2025.

GLP-1 receptor agonists and tirzepatide represent a promising therapeutic advance for obesity-related HFpEF. Benefits are likely mediated through weight loss dependent and weight-loss independent mechanisms. Important uncertainties remain regarding their role in non-obese HFpEF, optimal patient selection, and their safety in HFrEF.

artigos.titulo: Bariatric Surgery as a Rescue Strategy After Semaglutide or Tirzepatide
artigos.autores: Aminian A, Hammad AF, Sadeghmousavi S et al.
artigos.destaque: Bariatric surgery was associated with clinically meaningful 2-year weight loss after semaglutide or tirzepatide intolerance or inadequate response, with RYGB potentially offering greater benefit after inadequate response.

resumo.texto: To evaluate 2-year weight loss after bariatric surgery among adults with intolerable adverse effects or inadequate weight loss with semaglutide or tirzepatide.
Semaglutide and tirzepatide are effective obesity medications, but intolerance and inadequate weight loss are common, creating uncertainty about next-step therapy.

This retrospective cohort included adults with BMI ≥35 kg/m² undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) or sleeve gastrectomy (SG) at Cleveland Clinic hospitals from 2018 to 2024. Electronic health record and dispensing data classified preoperative semaglutide or tirzepatide exposure and response. The primary outcome was estimated 2-year total body weight loss (TBWL), stratified by procedure and type 2 diabetes (T2DM) status.

Among 4929 patients, 4661 had no prior exposure (comparator group), 61 discontinued semaglutide or tirzepatide because of intolerable adverse effects, and 207 had inadequate weight-loss response. Before surgery, estimated 2-year medication-associated weight change was a 1.4% gain in the intolerance group and 1.5% TBWL in the inadequate-response group. After surgery, 2-year TBWL in the intolerance group was 27.9% and 22.7% after RYGB and 20.1% and 21.6% after SG among patients without and with T2DM, respectively. Corresponding estimates in the inadequate-response group were 35.8%, 27.4%, 14.3%, and 14.2%. For comparison, corresponding 2-year TBWL estimates in the comparator group were 33.3%, 28.7%, 23.6%, and 19.9%. In adjusted analysis of the inadequate-response group, RYGB was associated with greater 2-year TBWL than SG (32.7% vs. 17.8%; difference, 14.9 percentage points [95% CI, 13.1%-16.7%]).

Bariatric surgery was associated with clinically meaningful 2-year weight loss after semaglutide or tirzepatide intolerance or inadequate response, with RYGB potentially offering greater benefit after inadequate response.

artigos.titulo: Management of Obesity in Special Populations and Limited-Resource Settings: An Egyptian Medical Position Statement
artigos.autores: Hegazy MA, Mattar A, Shawky MM et al.
artigos.destaque: These recommendations provide a pragmatic framework for obesity/adiposity-based chronic disease management in Egypt, emphasizing affordable, patient-centered care, and clinical multidisciplinary collaboration and policy support.

resumo.texto: Obesity/adiposity-based chronic disease is a chronic progressive relapsing disease linked to several comorbidities, with rising prevalence in Egypt. Limited local guidelines and healthcare challenges necessitate evidence-based, culturally adapted strategies.

The Egyptian Medical Association for the Study of Obesity convened a clinical multidisciplinary panel to develop consensus recommendations. Evidence was synthesized from literature, prioritizing resource-limited settings and special situations.

Assessment: Move beyond Body Mass Index to include waist circumference, waist/height ratio, body composition, and screening for obesity-related complications and diseases. Lifestyle Interventions: a-Nutrition: Mediterranean/dietary approach to stop hypertension diets, slow eating, and supervised fasting (eg Ramadan and Christian). b-Activity: Culturally tailored approaches (eg prayer-time movement and Arabic apps). c-Behavior: Cognitive-behavioral therapy and family-inclusive support. Pharmacotherapy: Use of approved agents (orlistat, naltrexone/bupropion, liraglutide, semaglutide, and tirzepatide) according to obesity-related complications and diseases and age group. Avoid GLP-1, GLP-1/GIP analogues in patients with medullary thyroid cancer, and all agents during pregnancy. Bariatric Surgery: Indicated for body mass index ≥40 kg/m2 (or ≥35 with obesity-related complications and diseases), with lifelong micronutrient supplementation. Special Populations: a-Adolescents: Focus on growth, not only weight-loss; consider pharmacotherapy in different age groups. b-Elderly: Prioritize muscle preservation; avoid weight loss unless obesity-related complications and diseases exist. c-Pregnancy: No weight loss; delay postpartum interventions until lactation is established. Policy Actions: Mandate food labeling, tax sugar-sweetened beverages, and integrate obesity services into primary healthcare.

These recommendations provide a pragmatic framework for obesity/adiposity-based chronic disease management in Egypt, emphasizing affordable, patient-centered care, and clinical multidisciplinary collaboration and policy support.

artigos.titulo: Evaluating Fiscal Credibility Through the Lens of Durability: Value Decay in AI-Enabled Clinical Documentation
artigos.autores: Atiku S, Olakotan O
artigos.destaque: AI documentation tools risk becoming "zombie technologies", operationally active but fiscally hollow, because institutional extraction mechanisms cannibalise their intended value. Achieving true durability requires contractually ring-fencing efficiency dividends for workforce recovery and explicitly pricing the shadow labour of maintenance and human-in-the-loop verification. Because fiscal and ethical judgements may conflict, we recommend that their oversight operate as separate and independent functions. These findings have direct implications for health systems reform, particularly procurement governance, productivity policy, and workforce sustainability strategies for digital health.

resumo.texto: AI-enabled clinical documentation tools are deployed to mitigate workforce burnout, yet technical efficiency observed in short-term evaluations frequently fails to translate into sustained institutional value. This study evaluates the fiscal credibility of these tools through the lens of durability, investigating how their value is sustained, eroded, or transformed once routine implementation is established.

We employed a netnographic design to analyse professional discourse across seven healthcare subreddits. Using a custom harvesting protocol over a 24-month window (2024-2025), we screened 2645 text segments. A "Double-Lock" filtration system isolated 39 high-fidelity discursive incidents focusing on post-implementation sustainment. Data were analysed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis informed by an abductive logic.

Analysis reveals that durability failure is driven by three socio-organisational mechanisms of value decay rather than technical inadequacy. First, Incentive Conversion occurs when administrative actors capture efficiency gains to increase throughput via a Jevons Paradox effect, transforming workforce relief into labour intensification. Second, Maintenance Entropy creates a hidden maintenance debt through the gradual accumulation of unpriced articulation work. Third, Legitimacy Collapse occurs when the cognitive load of verification exceeds the clinician's bandwidth, leading to the rejection of the tool's epistemic authority.

AI documentation tools risk becoming "zombie technologies", operationally active but fiscally hollow, because institutional extraction mechanisms cannibalise their intended value. Achieving true durability requires contractually ring-fencing efficiency dividends for workforce recovery and explicitly pricing the shadow labour of maintenance and human-in-the-loop verification. Because fiscal and ethical judgements may conflict, we recommend that their oversight operate as separate and independent functions. These findings have direct implications for health systems reform, particularly procurement governance, productivity policy, and workforce sustainability strategies for digital health.

artigos.titulo: How social media-induced secondary traumatic stress affects depression: a moderated mediation model of self-compassion and problematic social media use in college students
artigos.autores: Zhu S, Zhou J, Liu X
artigos.destaque: Moreover, the effect of self-compassion on depression was moderated by PSMU, with the effect being stronger for students with high PSMU (b = -0.32, p < .001) than those with low PSMU (b = -0.12, p < .001).Conclusions: STS-SM contributed to increased depressive symptoms by reducing individuals' levels of self-compassion, with the effect of self-compassion on depression moderated by PSMU. These findings underscore the importance of regulating traumatic content online and highlight self-compassion training as a promising intervention, particularly for those with PSMU.

resumo.texto: Background: Social media use has grown rapidly among college students, who constitute one of the most active user groups. However, exposure to negative and traumatic content on social media may lead to secondary traumatic stress (STS-SM), which may be linked to depression. This study examines the psychological mechanisms underlying the relationship between STS-SM and depressive symptoms among Chinese college students.Methods: A total of 1080 Chinese college students (382 females and 698 males; mean age = 19.07 years, SD = 1.08) completed web-based questionnaires including Secondary Traumatic Stress Scale for Social Media, Beck Depression Inventory-II, Self-compassion scale, and Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale. Age, gender, educational level, marital status, ethnicity, and subjective socioeconomic status were treated as covariates. Mediation and moderation analyses were performed to examine the role of self-compassion and problematic social media use (PSMU) in the relation between STS-SM and depression using the PROCESS macro in SPSS.Results: STS-SM was found to be positively associated with depression (r = 0.48, p < .001), and this correlation was mediated by self-compassion (b = 0.09, 95% CI [0.07, 0.11]). Moreover, the effect of self-compassion on depression was moderated by PSMU, with the effect being stronger for students with high PSMU (b = -0.32, p < .001) than those with low PSMU (b = -0.12, p < .001).Conclusions: STS-SM contributed to increased depressive symptoms by reducing individuals' levels of self-compassion, with the effect of self-compassion on depression moderated by PSMU. These findings underscore the importance of regulating traumatic content online and highlight self-compassion training as a promising intervention, particularly for those with PSMU.

artigos.titulo: Epigenetic aging during the COVID-19 pandemic: A prospective longitudinal study with prepandemic baseline data in children, adolescents, and adults
artigos.revista: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
artigos.autores: Schowe AM, Ruks M, Disselkamp CKL et al.
artigos.destaque: In adolescents, higher perceived pandemic burden was associated with a larger increase in pace of aging (DunedinPACE: b = 0.04, P = 0.01). Together, these findings suggest that prepandemic individual risk factors for poorer physical and mental health are accompanied by measurable increases in epigenetic aging during the COVID-19 pandemic, with adolescence representing a sensitive phase to its psychosocial burden.

resumo.texto: Psychosocial stress is a risk factor for aging-related diseases. The COVID-19 pandemic placed a psychosocial burden on individuals, potentially increasing the risk for aging-related diseases for which epigenetic clocks are used as early biomarkers. Based on four epigenetic clocks (DunedinPACE, GrimAge2, Horvath, and PedBE), we investigated whether epigenetic aging changed during the pandemic and whether these changes were associated with objective and subjective pandemic-related stressors and preexisting individual risk factors for poorer physical and mental health. We used prospective longitudinal data (n = 1,028), including repeated salivary DNA collection from children (n = 359, MAGE = 9.5 y), adolescents (n = 385, MAGE = 15.5 y), and adults (n = 284, MAGE = 24.3 y). Saliva was collected before the first phase of containment measures in Germany in March 2020 and after the second phase in 2021. We observed significant increases in epigenetic age acceleration (PedBE: b = 0.17, P < 0.0001; GrimAge2: b = 0.08, P < 0.0001) and pace of aging (DunedinPACE: b = 0.13, P < 0.0001) across all age groups. Prepandemic physical health and parental socioeconomic status, but not objective pandemic stressors, were significantly associated with this change. In adolescents, higher perceived pandemic burden was associated with a larger increase in pace of aging (DunedinPACE: b = 0.04, P = 0.01). Together, these findings suggest that prepandemic individual risk factors for poorer physical and mental health are accompanied by measurable increases in epigenetic aging during the COVID-19 pandemic, with adolescence representing a sensitive phase to its psychosocial burden.

artigos.titulo: Sex-dependent behavioral effects of chronic unpredictable stress in mice reveal methodological challenges in the assessment of stress-related phenotypes in females
artigos.autores: Sales AJ, Pedrazzi JFC, Silveira JR et al.
artigos.destaque: These findings indicate that behavioral endpoints validated in male rodents may not show comparable sensitivity in females and highlight the importance of considering baseline behavioral characteristics, estrous cycle stage, and sucrose concentration when designing and interpreting chronic stress studies.

resumo.texto: Chronic unpredictable stress (CUS) is widely used to model depression-like behaviors in rodents. However, its validation has been established in male animals, and its applicability to females remains poorly characterized.

We evaluated the validity of a CUS protocol in male and female Balb/c mice using the sucrose preference test (SPT), forced swim test (FST), elevated plus maze (EPM), open field test (OFT), and integrated emotionality z-scores. Predictive validity was assessed using different imipramine treatment schedules. Additional experiments examined the influence of sucrose concentration and estrous cycle stage on basal sucrose preference in females.

In male mice, 21 days of CUS reduced sucrose preference and emotionality z-scores. Chronic imipramine treatment initiated during the last 14 days of stress exposure prevented these behavioral alterations and reduced immobility time in the FST, whereas no significant effects were detected in the EPM. In female mice, CUS did not induce changes in sucrose preference or emotionality z-scores, although imipramine reduced immobility in the FST.

Although CUS protocols are widely validated in male rodents, the protocol showed limited sensitivity in females. Basal sucrose preference was influenced by estrous cycle stage and sucrose concentration, with reduced preference during periovulatory and greater preference during post-ovulatory stages only when sucrose was 2%.

These findings indicate that behavioral endpoints validated in male rodents may not show comparable sensitivity in females and highlight the importance of considering baseline behavioral characteristics, estrous cycle stage, and sucrose concentration when designing and interpreting chronic stress studies.

artigos.titulo: Baicalein Protects against Repeated Unpredictable Stress-Induced Depression-like Behavior in Mice
artigos.autores: Tang D, Shi Y, Zhou W et al.
artigos.destaque: These results suggest that baicalein may safeguard mice from depression- and anxiety-like behaviors precipitated by chronic stress, potentially through the augmentation of monoamine levels by inhibiting monoamine oxidase activity, and by stimulating the production of cyclic adenosine monophosphate and brain-derived neurotrophic factor in brain areas implicated in emotional disorders. Baicalein could prove to be a significant agent for the prevention or mitigation of the multifaceted symptoms associated with depression and anxiety.

resumo.texto: Baicalein, an active flavonoid derived from the root of Scutellaria baicalensis, has been extensively utilized in the treatment of stress-related neuropsychiatric disorders, encompassing behaviors indicative of depression and anxiety.
